posts.title: Stepping down as Editor-in-Chief of JOSS
posts.description: The picnic bench at Mt Carmel Junction, Utah, where JOSS was launched from – May 2016. Ten years ago this month, I announced a small experiment on this blog: a developer-friendly journal for research software, built around GitHub, with a review process that treated software as a first-class research output rather than an afterthought. posts.title: Chatops-Driven Publishing
posts.description: JOSS is coming up on it’s third birthday, and today we published our 500th paper . This has been no small feat and I’m hugely indebted to our wonderful group of volunteer editors and reviewers who have made all this possible. posts.title: Announcing The Journal of Open Source Software
posts.description: The Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) is a new take on an idea that’s been gaining some traction over the last few years, that is, to publish papers about software.
